name: The Jobs That Vanished
description: Lamplighters, knockers-up and human computers: the trades that once kept the world running and the machines that ended them.

checkpoints.name: Trades of the ancient world
checkpoints.note: Scribes recorded taxes and stories, smiths worked iron, and gladiators fought in Roman arenas. Work was tied to the needs of kings, temples and cities, and few people could choose their trade.

checkpoints.name: Knights, poets and barbers
checkpoints.note: Troubadours sang in the courts of southern France, barber surgeons let blood, and samurai served Japanese lords, each trade with its own tools, guild rules and place in society.

checkpoints.name: Craft and soot
checkpoints.note: Coopers made barrels, chimney sweeps climbed flues, lamplighters walked the streets, and human computers did the arithmetic of astronomers by hand, often for scientific tables that took many months to complete.

checkpoints.name: The machine age
checkpoints.note: The Pony Express, gandy dancers and knockers-up came with railways and factories, and the first telephone exchanges needed women to connect each call.

checkpoints.name: The last of them
checkpoints.note: Alarm clocks, automatic exchanges, electric lights and computers ended these jobs, and the milk float and the lamplighter faded to memory, though some towns keep a few as living history.
